title: R Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Show text
examples.description: cat joins values and writes them out. A backslash-n adds a new line.

examples.title: Name a value
examples.description: The <- arrow assigns a value to a name. Here pencils keeps the number 3.

examples.title: Keep several numbers
examples.description: A vector is an ordered group of values. c combines values into a vector.

examples.title: Read a position
examples.description: Square brackets select values. Position 2 is the second item in R.

examples.title: Do maths on a vector
examples.description: R can apply arithmetic to each value in a vector.

examples.title: Keep matching values
examples.description: A logical test makes true-or-false values. Use them in brackets to keep matching numbers.

examples.title: Find a mean
examples.description: mean adds values and divides by their count. This is the average.

examples.title: Handle missing data
examples.description: NA marks a missing value. is.na detects it.

examples.title: Make a data table
examples.description: A data frame stores columns of the same row count. Each column has a name.
examples.code:
books <- data.frame(title = c("Moon", "Sun"), pages = c(24, 30))
cat(books$pages, "\n")

examples.title: Name a calculation
examples.description: function defines reusable steps. R returns its final expression.

examples.title: Choose a message
examples.description: if checks one true-or-false value. else chooses the other action.
examples.code:
score <- 8
if (score >= 5) { cat("Pass\n") } else { cat("Try again\n") }

examples.title: Put values in order
examples.description: sort returns a vector in order from smallest to largest by default.
